recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-13167 unless the Patient Care work group later decides to broaden threading semantics for CommunicationRequest, which was not part of this issue's final applied resolution.
issue_request: FHIR-13167 was a Published/Persuasive Patient Care change request asking that asynchronous Communication conversations be threadable. The final resolution was to add Communication.inResponseTo as Reference(Communication) with cardinality 0..*.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied by bac396f21d6dc845c746e29a9fb7c79e27ee6ff5, whose subject explicitly names #13167 and whose patch added Communication.inResponseTo to the historical Communication spreadsheet source. The current XML StructureDefinition is a later refactor of that applied element.
additional_context: The Jira description mentioned CommunicationRequest, but the final resolution text narrowed the required element to Communication. Current source/fhir.ini actively includes both Communication and CommunicationRequest in the build. CommunicationRequest has request-chain elements such as basedOn and replaces, but no CommunicationRequest.inResponseTo; that absence matches the final resolution. A later applied issue, FHIR-40639, added the default Communication in-response-to search parameter for the same element, and that source is already present.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active Communication StructureDefinition already has Communication.inResponseTo 0..* Reference(Communication), and the active Communication search-parameter bundle includes the corresponding in-response-to search parameter.

related_jiras.note: Later Applied issue that added the default Communication in-response-to search parameter for Communication.inResponseTo.
